core_obligations: At a point where the sequence is regular in the fibre, use the relative dimension to obtain an inequality relating the dimension of the quotient ring to the length of the sequence (proof lines 33494-33512).

Spread that inequality to a neighbourhood using that the dimension function is upper semicontinuous and the length of the sequence is fixed, and conclude regularity there by the Cohen-Macaulay criterion (proof lines 33512-33520).
proof_roadmap: Turn regularity at the point into a numerical inequality (proof lines 33494-33512).
Spread the inequality out and apply the criterion (proof lines 33512-33521).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite type map with Cohen-Macaulay equidimensional fibres of dimension d, the set of points where a fixed sequence is regular in the fibre is open (statement lines 33478-33492). The proof does not work with the regularity condition directly: it converts regularity at a point into a numerical inequality involving the relative dimension, spreads that inequality to a neighbourhood using upper semicontinuity of the dimension function, and recovers regularity by the Cohen-Macaulay criterion (proof lines 33494-33521). Replacing regularity by a semicontinuous numerical condition is the step that makes openness visible. H2.
